text:
jess_support: Customer reported spike in latency then malformed completions after a failover. They were in eu-west, request id req_0b3f9a. Response suddenly came back from a different variant and function-calls disappeared. Sending logs. @mike_oncall

deploy-bot: Auto-failover triggered: eu-west-1 -> us-central due to capacity_shortage_2026-03-16. selected_variant=redwood-2.1-quant

mike_oncall: grabbing logs now. can you paste full request headers + model param?

jess_support: headers:
```
X-Region: eu-west-1
X-Request-ID: req_0b3f9a
Authorization: Bearer redacted
model: redwood-2.1
```

customer-app-team: we didn't set region explicitly — rely on routing. After the incident the response body included `model: redwood-2.1-quant` and tokens looked off (we saw weird leading bytes like "ĠHello" doubled). Also function-calling payload vanished.

anna_ml: :eyes: the `-quant` variant was built with an older tokenizer (bpe-v1) and a lightweight function-call shim was not compiled in. that can cause both tokenization drift and missing function-wrapper behavior. need full request/response to confirm.

ryan_sre: quick excerpt from serve logs for req_0b3f9a:
```
[2026-03-16T18:12:43Z] route: eu-west-1 -> us-central; reason=capacity_shortage; selected_variant=redwood-2.1-quant; routing_policy=auto_failover_any_variant
```
This shows the routing policy allowed any variant (no tokenizer/capability checks).

jess_support: repro steps I used:
1) POST /v1/generate (no region header) with `model=redwood-2.1` and a few-shot prompt that expects function calling
2) hit capacity in eu-west, auto-failover fires
3) response comes back from `redwood-2.1-quant` and is missing the `tool_call` wrapper. payload attached (shortened).

anna_ml: likely cause = capability mismatch + tokenizer drift between variants. Short-term mitigation: exclude quant variants from failover for this model family or prefer variants with `tokenizer_version==v2` and `supports_function_calls==true`. Longer term: add compatibility metadata to model catalog and enforce at routing time.

mike_oncall: can we add a temporary rule to block variant `redwood-2.1-quant` for customer `cust_42`? I can push an ACL to routing.

ryan_sre: pushed exclusion rule for cust_42 and blacklisted redwood-2.1-quant for that account. also purged KV caches related to req_0b3f9a. monitor now.

customer-app-team: after the block responses look normal again, latency back to baseline, function-calls present. thanks. :tada:

anna_ml: recommended next steps:
- immediate: add per-account variant exclusion for affected customers (done)
- 24-48h hotfix: enforce variant compatibility checks before selecting fallback (tokenizer_version + capability flags)
- 3-5d: model-catalog augmentation + rollout to all routing policies + tests that run synthetic few-shot/function-call prompts to detect regressions

jess_support: opened ENG-RUNTIME-612 with logs, repro steps, and routing trace. tagging @anna_ml @ryan_sre. customer asking for ETA and a short mitigation guide.

anna_ml: ETA: hotfix to routing (compatibility gate) ~24-48h, full catalog + gating ~3-5 days. In the meantime advise customers to pin `region=eu-west-1` or set `routing_preference=local` and to avoid relying on unspecified variant fallback. share short config snippet:
```
# recommended temporary client config
POST /v1/generate
Headers: {"X-Region":"eu-west-1"}
Body: {"model":"redwood-2.1","routing_preference":"local"}
```

ryan_sre: note: billing impact — cross-region failover incurred egress charges. @finance-bot please flag cust_42 for billing audit.

finance-bot: logged billing impact for cust_42 (egress during 2026-03-16 cross-region failover). will follow up separately.

jess_support: I'll send a customer-facing summary with the short-term configs, the exclusion we applied, and the ETA for the hotfix. closing the immediate loop. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
